shorts.title: What you will learn: Common mistakes and exam questions
shorts.script: Six traps that fail exams. Today is a safety walk through the traps. Exams and interviews love them, and now you can avoid every one. Most wrong answers come from a few old traps. Integer division drops the decimals. A small type wraps around when it is too small. A double is not exact, so equals can fail. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Common mistakes and exam questions.

shorts.title: Common mistakes and exam questions in one minute
shorts.hook: Most wrong answers come from a few old traps.
shorts.script: Most wrong answers come from a few old traps. Integer division drops the decimals. A small type wraps around when it is too small. A double is not exact, so equals can fail. Also, never return a reference to a local variable. Never use a moved object. Never forget to free what you made with new. Both numbers are ints, so the answer is an int. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Common mistakes and exam questions in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: A double stores a close value, and not the exact value.
shorts.script: A double stores a close value, and not the exact value. So the test with equals is false. Instead, take the difference. If its size is smaller than a tiny epsilon, the numbers are equal for our purpose. This test is true. The program prints three, then four, then false, and then true. Integer division drops the decimals. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A reference to a local variable
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in common mistakes and exam questions?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in common mistakes and exam questions? Bug of the Day. The function returns a reference to a local variable. The compiler warns that it returns a reference to a local variable. The variable dies at the end of the function. Return by value. The local variable dies when the function ends, so the reference points to nothing. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A reference to a local variable.
